claims.statement: The European Commission estimates building-efficiency investment needs at 242 billion euros per year from 2021 to 2030 and describes national renovation plans as a way to establish predictable project pipelines.

The revised Energy Performance of Buildings Directive introduces staged solar-readiness and installation requirements for several classes of new, renovated, and public buildings where suitable and feasible.

contrary_evidence: Local engineering firms already prepare audits and tenders, often through relationship-based processes.
Housing-cooperative board decisions can remain slow even when analysis is improved.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with one regional property manager and 5-10 buildings, using family-company contractors only as transparent market participants.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 5000 active buildings at 1800 PLN annual net revenue yield 9m PLN ARR; at 35% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 55% founder ownership, equity is about 6.9m PLN in year 7-10, without separately counting retained earnings.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15-20 hours weekly in the pilot, with engineering review purchased per project rather than hired full-time.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 72-82% after document processing and customer success; licensed engineers remain external to the software fee.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 10000-25000 PLN to onboard a manager, recovered from 10-15 active buildings within 12 months.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 1500-3000 PLN per active building per year, with portfolio minimums and no hidden contractor commission.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Managers retain annual portfolio records while each building cycles through audits, tenders, maintenance, and later renovations.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Comparable scopes, regional bid data, change orders, and realized outcomes improve estimates and vendor benchmarking
fingerprint.customer: Housing cooperatives and multi-building owners administered by professional property managers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Property managers and housing associations roll the workflow across their recurring building portfolios
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Neutral renovation procurement and decision-support operating system with fixed, disclosed software fees
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Manager or building pays an annual project-workspace fee for each active building
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A board or owner must scope, compare, approve, and track a renovation across fragmented vendors and documents

founder_fit: Local access to renewable contractors helps build realistic templates and bid normalization.
Document automation and comparative analysis suit an AI-leveraged, analytical founder.
Portfolio distribution through managers replaces repeated one-building-at-a-time selling.
risks: Procurement rules and engineering liability vary by project.
A transaction marketplace could undermine trust if fee disclosure is weak.
Long renovation cycles delay proof of ROI and revenue recognition.

structure.control_point: Comparable scope, bid, approval, and outcome record across managed buildings
structure.critical_dependency: A property manager willing to standardize its renovation process across multiple buildings

thesis: Give property managers and housing-cooperative associations a portfolio workflow that turns bills and building records into comparable retrofit scopes, standardized requests for quote, bid normalization, board-ready decision packs, and post-project tracking. Managers distribute it across buildings they repeatedly serve; the product remains a neutral software system paid by the building or manager, rather than an undisclosed lead seller.
title: Housing-Manager Renovation Tender OS
uncertainties: Whether managers will pay centrally or pass a per-building fee to owners.
Which document and bid formats recur often enough to standardize first in Poland.
Can the product stay neutral while contractors demand paid access to tenders?
